Covariance of the coefficients of a fast AME fit

Source: R/ame_als_vcov.R
vcov.ame_als.Rd

Returns the covariance matrix of every regression coefficient of an ame_als or lame_als fit: the intercept, the dyadic coefficients and the node-covariate coefficients.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ame_als'
vcov(object, ...)

Arguments

object

an ame_als fit.

...

ignored.

Value

A covariance matrix with matching row/column names, covering every coefficient of coef().

Details

Every fit the fast route returns is an empirical-Bayes fit (see ame_als), and its covariance is the Laplace covariance: the inverse of the penalised Fisher information of all the parameters (the coefficients, the actor effects, the node-covariate coefficients and the latent factors) at the final weights (for a normal fit the exact information of the Gaussian cell, whose Laplace approximation is exact for the coefficients and the effects), with the actor effects' covariance fit$eb$sab and the factor scales held at their estimates. It propagates the uncertainty of the actor effects and the factors. The covariance conditional on the factors is fit$eb$vcov_cond. A fit an earlier release made with a setting this release no longer has stops with an error of class lame_als_removed_setting; refit it with ame_als or lame_als.

A bootstrap attached to the fit (bootstrap = N) takes precedence: its covariance is that of the replicates, and a coefficient the bootstrap gives no standard error for (see ame_als_bootstrap) keeps its analytic variance, with zero covariance with the others (fit$bootstrap$se_source names it).

See also

ame_als_bootstrap for bootstrap uncertainty.
